co_authors.description: user IDs of humans who instructed the task; written as Co-authored-by trailers of their own GitHub identity (each at most once: params_invalid otherwise)

signing.description: none, or the committer identity's own SSH signing key (default: key when it has one)

merge.description: create the merge commit of the session's prepared merge (github.merge_base) with two parents; not with paths (ADR-084 section 4)

decisions.description: only with merge: the choice for every conflict without markers and for every merged path that was changed on purpose

params_subagent_instruct.description: a follow-up instruction for a running child session of the requesting session (ADR-088 section 1)

params_subagent_stop.description: ends a running child session of the requesting session (ADR-088 section 1)

title.description: 1-120 characters, single line (no control characters, no line or paragraph separator)

result_github_get_pull_request.description: patches at most 1 MiB in total; truncated when patches were left out; mergeable and mergeable_state as GitHub computes them (KOR-48, ADR-084 section 2): null while GitHub still computes it after the device read again after 1 s and 2 s, false = conflict with the base; absent in results of older runners

mergeable_state.description: GitHub's word (clean, dirty, draft, unknown, blocked, behind, unstable, has_hooks, ...); display only

merge_parent.description: the second parent of a merge commit (the merged base tip)

result_github_create_pull_request.description: existing true: an open PR with the same head/base was found (MCP status duplicate)

result_subagent_instruct.description: the child's guest registered the instruction; instruction_id = the operation ID (get_subagent_result)

result_subagent_stop.description: the child's state after the stop (stopping while its guest cannot be reached)

workvm_id.description: ID of a work VM (13-work-vm.md section 1)

workvm_size.description: standard 4 CPU/8 GiB/50 GiB, large 8/16/100, xlarge 16/32/200 (13-work-vm.md section 2)

workvm_scope.description: task: the VM of the task, shared by its sessions; session: a VM of the requesting session only

created.description: false: the existing VM of the scope was returned

test_run_kind.description: what the run checks; a label for people and lists (ADR-080 section 1)

test_run_state.description: running while it runs; passed = exit code 0, failed = another exit code, timed_out = the time limit ended it, cancelled = ended by the platform (credit), error = the platform could not run it

test_run_reason.description: why a run ended error or cancelled; null otherwise

test_run_summary.description: counts read from a summary line the runner recognises; null when there is none

log_ref.description: the complete output as an encrypted log object (GET /v1/tasks/{task}/logs/{object}); truncated: only the last stored_bytes of bytes are kept

browser_id.description: ID of a platform browser session (13-work-vm.md section 13.1)

browser_close_reason.description: why a browser session ended or its VM was replaced (13-work-vm.md section 13.2); null while open

created.description: false: the open browser session of the session was returned

closed.description: false: nothing was open (reason: how the last one ended, or null)

result_github_list_issues.description: one page of the repository's issues; per_page and page count issues (pull requests, which GitHub lists among the issues, are left out and do not count), so a page is empty only when there are no further issues; truncated: entries that did not fit the contract were left out or titles were cut, or the flood limit ended the reading (then note says how to go on)

items.description: label name (GitHub allows at most 50 characters)

next_page.description: the page to ask for next, null on the last page

note.description: present when the flood limit ended the reading before the page was complete (how to reach the issues beyond it) or when the page did not fit one result and lost its last issues (ask with a smaller per_page)

result_github_get_issue.description: an issue with one page of its comments (oldest first); the result stays within 200 KiB of JSON (newest comments of the page, then the body are cut first, truncated)

items.description: label name (GitHub allows at most 50 characters)

pull_request.description: the number belongs to a pull request (read it with github.get_pull_request)

comments_next_page.description: the page to ask for next, null on the last page

result_github_list_pull_requests.description: one page of the repository's pull requests

next_page.description: the page to ask for next, null on the last page

result_github_request_connection.description: the task owner's connected GitHub account; while the owner is not connected the platform holds the request and asks the owner to connect (KOR-25)

params_human_question.description: human.question (KOR-39, ADR-076 section 3): a main session asks a person; the task waits in needs_decision/question until the next prompt answers it

question.description: the question to the person, 1-4000 characters (line breaks allowed); sealed in operation.params

params_human_approval.description: human.approval (KOR-39, ADR-076 section 3): as human.question, the person approves or declines (needs_decision/approval)

question.description: the question to the person, 1-4000 characters (line breaks allowed); sealed in operation.params

result_github_list_identities.description: the GitHub identities the human the session works for may use in this task, the one that applies now and the humans that may be named as co-authors (ADR-078)

signing.description: the identity holds an own signing key

source.description: why the human may use it

discard.description: replace uncommitted changes in the workspace directory on purpose (default false: workspace_dirty)

merge_conflict_kind.description: content: conflict markers in the file; without markers (a decision of the merge commit is needed): binary (head's version kept), modify_delete (modified version kept), type (file against directory: head's entries kept), mode (added on both sides with different modes: head's mode), protected (a protected name, link or submodule: head's entry kept) (ADR-084 section 4)

base_sha.description: the tip of the base branch that was merged

up_to_date.description: the head already contains the base tip; the workspace was not touched

result_github_list_reviews.description: GitHub's reviews of the pull request (newest 100) and the platform verdicts the device knows for it within the session's reach

profile.description: the name of the session's effective rights profile when it gave the verdict, null without (ADR-091 section 5)

github_identity.description: the GitHub identity to act with (ADR-078 section 3); must be usable by the human the session works for

result_github_get_checks.description: the check runs and commit statuses of the commit ref names; state failure when one finished unsuccessfully, pending while one is not finished, success when every one succeeded, none without any

params_review_verdict.description: review.verdict (KOR-51, ADR-091 section 4): a review session's verdict on one head of a pull request; sealed in operation.params

profile.description: the name of the session's effective rights profile when it gave the verdict, null without (ADR-091 section 5)

params_security_report.description: security.report (KOR-51, ADR-091 section 4): the structured result of a security scan
